# What Netlify authentication tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters and so is a whole token body — the shortest one the
# pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is spelled in lowercase where
# the case does not matter and in uppercase where the case is what a case is
# about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either spelling is a body.

patterns: netlify-auth-token

# The five kinds Netlify issues in this format. Each is nf, one character naming
# the kind and an underscore, and behind that the same body, so what the
# character says is which kind a token is and not what the token may reach.

case:     a personal access token
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a netlify cli token
in:       nfc_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     an oauth access token
in:       nfo_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     an app.netlify.com token
in:       nfu_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a build token
in:       nfb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

# The places a token is written.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=«netlify-auth-token»

case:     a token in the config file the netlify cli logs in to
in:       {"users":{"0123":{"auth":{"token":"nfc_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"}}}}
out:      {"users":{"0123":{"auth":{"token":"«netlify-auth-token»"}}}}

case:     a token in the authorization header a request to the api carries
in:       Authorization: Bearer nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      Authorization: Bearer «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a token on a command line
in:       netlify deploy --prod --auth nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      netlify deploy --prod --auth «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a token in a workflow environment block
in:       env:\n  NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN: nfb_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      env:\n  NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN: «netlify-auth-token»

# The alphabet the thirty-six characters are written in. Netlify names none, and
# base62 — the letters of both cases and the digits — is what the format's own
# shape asks for: the alphabet that adds the underscore to base62 is base64url,
# which adds the hyphen with it, and a body admitting the underscore would carry
# the character the prefix is read off by. Either of the two ends a body here.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       nfp_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdef-ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      nfp_0123456789abcdef-ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdef_ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      nfp_0123456789abcdef_ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

# The lengths either side of thirty-six. Netlify states one number, that a field
# holding a token needs room for forty characters, and writes its prefixes with
# no underscore in them; the thirty-six behind a four-character prefix is read
# off the tokens instead, and comes to that forty. Like the npm and GitHub
# bodies and unlike the AWS access key ID, it is read as a floor rather than a
# count: thirty-five characters are not a token, and thirty-seven are one token
# to the end of its run rather than a token and a character left over. What the
# floor costs is the middle case below — a token cut short of thirty-six keeps
# every random character written in front of the cut, and none of them is
# redacted.

case:     a body of thirty-six characters is a token
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a body of thirty-five characters is not
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy
out:      nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxy

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a token to the end of it
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts — and where the run of its alphabet carries on past
# the floor, what carries it on is redacted with the token. A hyphen and an
# underscore end the run instead.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       NETLIFY_TOKEN_nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      NETLIFY_TOKEN_«netlify-auth-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xnfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      x«netlify-auth-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzsuffix
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a token
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz-suffix
out:      «netlify-auth-token»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a token
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_suffix
out:      «netlify-auth-token»_suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz.
out:      the token is «netlify-auth-token».

# Two tokens written together, which merge for two different reasons. The three
# characters in front of the underscore belong to the alphabet a body is written
# in, so a body may close with nf and a kind character and the underscore of the
# next token stand directly behind it; the second token then begins three
# characters before the first one ends, and the two spans overlap. Two tokens
# written straight against each other merge as well, and the reason there is
# that a span reaches the end of its run: the first token's run carries on
# through the nf and the kind character of the second prefix and stops at that
# prefix's underscore, so the first span already covers where the second one
# begins. Parted by anything a run does not admit, they are two values and both
# go.

case:     a token beginning inside the token before it
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwnfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyznfo_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     two tokens of different kinds separated by a space
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz nfb_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
out:      «netlify-auth-token» «netlify-auth-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix carries an
# underscore, which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding
# can hold one. Where thirty-six base62 characters follow, the run from the
# prefix to the end of them is redacted whether or not Netlify issued it. That
# is the answer rather than a fault in it, because such a run is a
# token's format exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart: sparing
# these would spare a real token written the same way. What is taken is a
# stretch of a value that was already opaque to a reader.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzznfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«netlify-auth-token»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzznfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«netlify-auth-token»

# A digest written behind the prefix. Hexadecimal digits are base62 and a digest
# carries nothing that ends a run, so a prefix and the forty characters of a
# SHA-1 are a token's format exactly, as a prefix and the sixty-four of a
# SHA-256 are. Both are redacted. Declining them would mean declining every
# token Netlify happened to write in the digits alone, which is a whole
# credential against a cache key. What holds either side of it is the floor and
# the prefix: an MD5 is thirty-two characters, four short of a body, and a
# hyphen is no character a prefix carries.

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a sha256 in a cache key
in:       key: nfp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «netlify-auth-token»

case:     an md5 behind the prefix, four characters short of a body
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      nfp_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha1 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       nfp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      nfp-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The prefix is held to the case Netlify
# writes it in, to all four of its characters, and to naming one of the five
# kinds — which is what a name opening nfs_ rests on. A digest and a sentence
# hold no underscore where a prefix wants one, so they hold no position to be
# found at however long they run; the names Unicode normalization code is
# written with do carry a prefix, and what turns them away is the next
# underscore of the name, which ends the run long before thirty-six characters
# of it have been read.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       NFP_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      NFP_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a hyphen where the prefix carries an underscore
in:       nfp-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      nfp-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a character naming no kind
in:       nfs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      nfs_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       nfp_0123456789abcdef ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      nfp_0123456789abcdef ghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz

case:     a hexadecimal digest
in:       sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     the names unicode normalization code is written with
in:       nfc_normalized = nfc_normalize(nfc_quick_check(input_string))
out:      nfc_normalized = nfc_normalize(nfc_quick_check(input_string))

# And a Netlify credential this pattern has nothing to say about. The format
# this one replaced carried no prefix and nothing of its own to be recognised
# by, so the only thing left to locate one by is the word Netlify standing near
# it, which is a rule about the text around a value rather than about the value.
# Netlify has left those tokens working, so what stands here is a live
# credential the library does not redact.

case:     a token of the format netlify issued before this one
in:       NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab
out:      NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ab

# Further text shapes a token is written in, and further adjacency the prefix
# and the run carry no boundary against.

case:     a token in a netrc entry
in:       machine api.netlify.com login user password nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
out:      machine api.netlify.com login user password «netlify-auth-token»

case:     a token in a url query string
in:       https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites?access_token=nfo_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz&page=2
out:      https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites?access_token=«netlify-auth-token»&page=2

case:     two tokens in parentheses
in:       (nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, nfb_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ)
out:      («netlify-auth-token», «netlify-auth-token»)

case:     a token followed by a carriage return and a newline
in:       NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=nfc_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\r\n
out:      NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN=«netlify-auth-token»\r\n

case:     a token between tabs
in:       \tnfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz\t
out:      \t«netlify-auth-token»\t

case:     a token between japanese
in:       日本語nfp_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz日本語
out:      日本語«netlify-auth-token»日本語
